one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 results are expected ~Nov 9-18. Correcting my round-1 claim: only the infrastructure section moved to quarterly, so a September production/BTC update is likely in mid-October. It should be low-impact; August showed 1,310 BTC at 79.9 EH/s, and with hashprice back near $39.6 a September print should be solid but expected. Other in-window drivers: the ~Oct 3 difficulty retarget (projected +0.4%); BTC (~$83-85k, stuck near $83k through late September per Polymarket commentary); the late-October FOMC (rate hikes are a headwind); and company news, either Tydal project financing (+) or ATM sales under the $1B program (-). There is no clear momentum signal after the drop from $12.97 to $10.64. So I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median $10.55 (a small tilt below spot for ATM supply) and monthly sigma 0.295, a bit below 108%/3.5 because no scheduled company event falls in the window. Rounds 3-4: the GPU-life rebuild, the site-by-site accounting and the split discount rate change long-dated values only; none of them is a scheduled October event, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site split-rate DCF (-$2.27, 25%), 2028E EV/EBITDA with risked pipeline NPVs ($9.83, 37.5%) and site-by-site SOTP ($3.90, 37.5%) = $4.58, down from $5.32. Every inventory site now appears once; contracted cash flows are discounted at 9.0% (LC-backed Tydal yrs 1-5, anchored on TeraWulf's 7.75% secured notes re-based to today's rates) or 11.0% (unrated: Volta yrs 6-10, GPU offtakes, A202 fee), everything else at the 12.5% WACC (mining 16%). Single-rate DCF -$2.77. Net debt $1.45B, 273M shares.

Carried 12m: EV x 1.125 - net debt $1.45B x 1.07 = -$0.62B / 273M = -$2.27. Single-rate (every non-mining cash flow at the 12.5% WACC, mining 16%): EV $708M -> -$2.77. bear.story: BTC back to $60-70k (Polymarket gave ~67% odds of touching $70k by year-end as of early Sept), so hashprice falls toward the $27.7 June low and mining FCF is near zero ahead of the 2028 halving. A201 is not signed and the GB300 racks go to lower-priced spot demand. Tydal project debt comes late or costs more, and with $491M of current related-party loans plus ~$1B of 2027 capex, heavy ATM dilution happens near the lows. GPU rents fall faster as Rubin supply arrives, the old H100-class fleet goes cash-neutral, and A202 sits empty while Bitdeer pays its ~$94M/yr facility fee; Knoxville and the US pipeline get no tenant.

base.story: BTC ~$80-95k. Tydal comes online by 2027-03-31 and is funded with project debt. A102 revenue starts Q1-2027, A201's committed 70% goes live in Q2-2027, and A202 is partly contracted, so its fee is mostly covered. Knoxville is still searching for customers. Dilution ~10-13%. The market values BTDR near segment-multiple value with a modest pipeline option, below round 3's $9.0 because the split-rate Tydal NPV and the A202 fee cut the floor value.

bull.story: BTC >$110k in the pre-halving run-up, plus a second Tydal-style lease at Rockdale (742 MW) Weathersfield or the Tydal expansion halls, A202 and Knoxville contracted at A201-like rates ($22M/MW), and Tydal project debt priced near 9%. The stock re-rates toward contracted-AI peers and the ~$22 consensus target.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$5 (market cap ~$1.37B) the market cap is about equal to net debt (~$1.45B), and EV (~$2.8B) covers only Tydal's split-rate NPV ($1.02B, ~$3.7/sh) plus mining at a trough multiple, with nothing for A201's committed $1.7B, A202, Knoxville or ~1.4 GW of uncontracted power. A sustained price there would most likely mean something fundamental broke: Volta's LC backstop or the Mar-2027 delivery failed, refinancing of the $491M of current BIT loans (13% effective) forced deeply dilutive equity, A201 commitments fell through, or hashprice went cash-negative. I keep $5.0: the split-rate Tydal value is lower than round 3's, but $5 is still where equity ~ net debt, and $5.3 would sit only ~0.65 sigma below spot.

reasoning: Round 4 (site accounting and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF site by site from the checked inventory (source 44). Mining now runs only on the 1,471 MW actually energized plus the 47 MW Massillon rebuild (85-90 EH/s); round 3's growth to 100 EH/s had no capex behind it. Fox Creek is a separate 60%-probability build that is NPV-negative at post-halving hashprice (-$26M). Knoxville, Wenatchee and Tydal are out of the mining base, and Rockdale's 563 MW stays mining with an HPC option only on the 179 MW expansion, so no MW is counted twice. No sites were sold. A202 is a cost commitment: Bitdeer pays an undisclosed 10-yr facility fee (I assume $120/kW-month, $94M/yr) from Q3-2027 in every branch, and the GPU-cloud upside is probability-weighted (40/25/35), so its value goes from $0.44B to $0.11B. Following the supervisor, leased halls (A101/A102/A201/A202) no longer get a shell-as-colocation terminal. A201 uses the 9/29 primary release ($340M/yr on the committed 70%, at 95%). Knoxville, Wenatchee, Tydal P3, Rockdale +179, Weathersfield and Clarington are each probability-weighted, net of capex, at 12.5% ($0.73B together). For discounting, Bitdeer has no secured debt priced against a contract, so I anchor on TeraWulf's 7.75% BB secured notes against Google-backstopped leases, re-based for a 10Y that is ~1.3 points higher: 9.0% for Tydal's LC-covered first five lease years, and 11.0% for unrated cash flows (Volta yrs 6-10, the GPU offtakes, the A202 fee). Tydal yrs 11-16, tails, pipeline and corporate stay at the 12.5% WACC. The split raises the DCF from -$2.77 (single rate) to -$2.27, but Tydal is worth less than round 3's $1.34B (all at 9%) because Volta is unrated and the LCs cover only ~28% of TCV. The EV/EBITDA leg rises to $9.83: A201 is priced at its signed terms ($22M/MW), the risked pipeline is now included, and the funding gap is issued at the leg's own value, not $10.5. The SOTP falls to $3.90 (split Tydal, A202 fee, site-by-site pipeline instead of $0.6M/MW). Fair value is $5.32 -> $4.58. Most of the change is long-dated and partly offsets, so I move the distribution only a little: bear $3.9/32%, base $8.6/45%, bull $21/23%, blended 50/50 with a lognormal (median $8.6, sigma 0.95). P(>=spot) goes 0.408 -> 0.383. The 1-month ladder and the $5.0 thesis break are unchanged. Searches this round: 2 (TeraWulf secured-note pricing; Johor colocation rates), plus 1 fetch of the A201 release. Round-4 sources are mostly primary filings for site facts, so the in-lane share is ~55%.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted cohorts at contract price for the term (A102/A201/A202 5 yrs, A101 to 2030); afterwards and for uncontracted GPUs rent = contract rate x P(age)/P(age at signing), P = 100/80/58/47/42/38/32/25/15/6% of launch level for chip ages 0-9 (steep ~25-30%/yr for 2 yrs, flat ~40% at yrs 3-5, then fade); runs while rent > site cost ($2.64M/MW leased Malaysia halls incl. $1.44M facility fee; $1.2M owned US sites) + 22% variable; 5-yr case compresses the curve by 6/5, 7-yr case stretches it by 6/7; refresh at end of life at $27.4M/MW capex, NPV-zero net of facility fee; no shell-as-colocation terminal for leased halls
gpu_life.note: Split-rate DCF (single-rate: -$3.37 / -$2.77 / -$2.23). Applies to the Malaysia AI cloud (A101/A102/A201/A202, legacy fleet), the Knoxville/Wenatchee cloud branches and, via tenant credit, Tydal (10% default at lease yr 6; 15% at yr 5 for 5-yr life, 7% at yr 7 for 7-yr). Company lives per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5; my 6 is the 5-yr contract plus a ~1-yr tail. The life spread is wider than in round 3 (+/-$0.6) because removing the shell floor leaves the cohort tail as the only post-contract value.

discounting.basis: Contracted, creditworthy: 9.0% for Tydal lease yrs 1-5, the period covered by ~$1.3B of letters of credit arranged by JPM-affiliated banks (AA range). Bitdeer has no debt priced against a contract (its only secured debt is the related-party BIT loan at 13.0% on general collateral), so the anchor is TeraWulf's $3.2B 7.75% BB-rated secured notes (Oct-2025) against 10-yr Fluidstack leases with a Google backstop, re-based from a ~4.0% to today's 5.29% 10Y. Contracted, unrated: 11.0% for Tydal yrs 6-10 (Volta is private and unrated; the LCs run down and are still 'anticipated'), for the term of the A101/A102/A201 GPU offtakes (customers undisclosed, ~50% of capex prepaid), and for the A202 facility fee Bitdeer owes. Uncontracted: 12.5% WACC for Tydal yrs 11-16 (no-fee walk right) and residual, GPU tails, A201's unsigned 30%, all pipeline sites and corporate; mining at 16% for BTC-cycle risk in both versions. The single-rate DCF puts every non-mining cash flow at 12.5%.
